canal_p08_001.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_001.text: The hearing began on the sixteenth morning with a kettle boiling too vigorously beneath the awning. Tian moved it away from the paper table before Pei arrived with the receiving schedule. People came carrying ordinary evidence in baskets, tins and folded sleeves. Han brought his claim copy without the personal chest. The broker stood at the far edge, interested but not appointed to speak for the bank. Yue placed three spare stools where late arrivals would not have to walk through somebody else's account.

canal_p08_002.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_002.text: Eighteen current households attended in person, five offered written replies, three remained away at seasonal work and two declined while asking for the resulting notice. The clerk recorded the actual participation. Their absence did not restore the expired pledge, and their replies would not be invented by neighbors. The charter's four current trustees all attended. Three formed the ordinary public reserve quorum after notice; today's recorded decision would use that authority. The hearing was open, but not every person in the yard had the same role.

canal_p08_003.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_003.text: Luo read the current gate and drain results before the disputed title. The new cap had passed its ordinary service checks; the drain's waterline had fallen after two obstructions were cleared. Current traffic still had its own delays, and the future higher-flow route remained untested. Yue had wanted the report to sound impressive. Luo kept it useful. A boatman's cough interrupted the last sentence, and the keeper waited rather than raising her voice until the cough became another reason to stop listening.

canal_p08_004.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_004.text: Tian read the expired successor-service notice while people still had the exact offending names in front of them. She described the six annual days assigned to her father's household and the sale lot's claim over her present hours. She did not attribute every damp room to Han. Her anger sounded stronger after she removed that borrowed accusation. Han sat with his hands flat on his knees, listening to the actual clause he had allowed beside his seal. He would have his answer after the original terms were read.

canal_p08_005.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_005.text: An Ru presented the certified original four annual seasons and the receiving comparison. The sixty accepted worker-days in each season made two hundred forty completed days. The founding emergency winter belonged inside the first season. No birth, death or marriage renewed the pledge, and later voluntary maintenance lists did not add successors to its debt terms. Pei held the public receiving page so its exterior references could be seen. The yard grew quiet as people recognized the heading they had never received on their copied household notices.

canal_p08_006.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_006.text: The daughter whose mother worked under her dead husband's name read the approved attribution correction. The seasonal total remained unchanged; the person finally named was the woman who had carried the wood. Her brother's extra copy had reached the ridge through the chosen messenger. She stopped after the name because her voice shook. Nobody filled the silence with a grander story. Pei waited beside her, and the daughter finished the one sentence she had come to say before taking her own copy home.

canal_p08_007.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_007.text: The clerk read the reed cutter's offered sentence in his requested voice. Present workers should be hired for current tasks, and the old account should not call his mother lucky to have been allowed to work. One trustee shifted in his chair. He had planned to describe the founding agreement as a gift to all households. Han said the timber helped them survive, which was true. Tian answered that help could leave a burden too. The chair kept both offered accounts beside the completed certificate instead of choosing the kinder adjective.

canal_p08_008.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_008.text: A household supporter of the sale asked whether the bank would refuse every buyer who offered improvements. The corrected title did not prohibit private loading contracts or future properly authorized services. It meant Han could not sell the canal bed, protected spill use or households' present hands under this pledge. An Ru showed the specific wording, not a rule that all money near common water became corrupt. The woman read it and said she would still prefer a dependable private drain contract to another neglected public schedule.

canal_p08_009.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_009.text: Luo accepted that preference and showed the drain's current receiver and next check. The woman wanted its later inspection performed, not merely listed. The keeper said the actual closure report would include the completed check when it happened. Han asked whether the room's old damage was part of his debt decision. The chair said the offered bills would be heard separately because their causes and remedies required different evidence. Yue watched the hearing resist the temptation to make one vote answer every grievance in the yard.

canal_p08_010.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_010.text: Han read his remaining monetary claim. His mother had advanced two hundred forty copper; cash repayments of one hundred twenty-eight and unused returned timber credit of thirty-two left eighty. The original toll-share right survived the completed labor and discharged movable-stock security. He did not claim the mother had been only kind, nor the bank only ungrateful. He asked for the proposed twenty-four payment now the supporting comparisons were complete. Tian looked at the clear account and nodded once, still angry about the sale list beside it.

canal_p08_011.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_011.text: The reserve keeper opened the earmarked account for comparison. Its one hundred twenty copper held ninety-six already committed to the repair order and twenty-four separately available for the proposed valid loan payment. Completed repair wages and supplied materials belonged inside the ninety-six. Current ordinary operation had its own budget and dated receipts. The keeper did not stack the same coin into both columns because a public hearing could make it look plentiful. Yue read the actual receipt references while another clerk checked the box against its current recorded balance.

canal_p08_012.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_012.text: One trustee wanted to hold the twenty-four for possible future storm damage instead. The loan was valid, but paying it today would reduce flexible reserve while the diversion route still needed work. The other trustees asked whether the accepted ninety-six repair order remained fully funded. It did. A larger emergency would need its own authorized source if it arose; the current proposal did not secretly buy that future response. The objection stayed in the decision record. A reasonable fear did not have to become a false account.

canal_p08_013.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_013.text: Han asked whether delaying again meant the bank could postpone his remaining eighty forever by naming another possible danger. The toll-share agreement allowed genuine essential operating costs, but not invented charges designed solely to avoid payment. An Ru described the specific payment proposal and future review, leaving the original limited right intact. The chair said the trustees would decide today's twenty-four under their actual authority. Yue could see Han preparing to argue the entire future. He took a breath and asked them to vote on the money presently before them.

canal_p08_014.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_014.text: Before that vote, the trustees recorded the completed pledge and rejected the canal-bed and successor-service sale lot under the original terms. All four supported removing those claims from the current notice. The private loading shed and specified equipment remained Han's, with their own agreements intact. The buyer's agent received the formal canceled-title finding already notified in preliminary form. Tian exhaled so sharply that Yue heard her above the awning's flap. The release did not depend on today's monetary vote or the later direction of flood water.

canal_p08_015.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_015.text: The payment proposal passed with three trustees supporting it and one opposing for the stated reserve concern. The public record preserved the vote rather than announcing unanimous household gratitude. Its authority came from the noticed charter procedure and actual quorum. The reserve keeper prepared the twenty-four transfer after checking the accepted resolution. Han received it in the yard and counted it with the clerk. His acknowledgment reduced the valid balance from eighty to fifty-six. An Ru witnessed the amount actually paid, not merely the hope attached to it.

canal_p08_016.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_016.text: Han put the twenty-four in his private receiving purse, where it became available for the deposit return rather than a new public repair supply. The future fifty-six remained subject to the original eligible toll receipts and conditions. The broker noted the paid installment without acquiring any right by watching it happen. Yue copied the signed receipt and gave Han his agreed counterpart. Tian asked whether he now withdrew every successor claim. He said the completed pledge gave him none, and signed that explicit correction beside his earlier seal.

canal_p08_017.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_017.text: The buyer's agent wanted Han to hand him the twenty-four immediately as part of his forty-eight private deposit. Han could choose an early partial return, but the agent's contract did not compel payment that moment. Han held the money while seeking the customer's eight and the surplus goods' sixteen so he could settle the whole amount together before the term's end. The agent entered that stated plan without calling it completed. The public hearing moved on. It had paid one valid debt installment, not become the receiver of all Han's private bargains.

canal_p08_018.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_018.text: A gust lifted the awning's open side while Pei was reading the amended notice. Bao signaled for the paper table to be covered and helped lower the flapping corner from the clear ground. Nobody stood on a stool beneath its pulling pole. A loose tie slipped, scattering two empty wrappers into the yard. Children chased them until Tian asked them to stop at the marked working space. The papers stayed dry and in order. The meeting paused for an ordinary hazard rather than waiting until a dramatic loss proved the wind mattered.

canal_p08_019.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_019.text: Rain began in a short hard shower that sounded louder against the awning than the speakers had. The trustees moved the remaining discussion into the keeper's store after its owner cleared a dry floor area. They took the accepted decisions and copies separately from the unused wrappers. Yue carried the comparison stack under its cover while Pei walked beside her with the receiving original. The sudden weather did not erase what had already been recorded. It changed the room in which they would hear the costs that a correct vote left behind.

canal_p08_020.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_020.text: The temporary check worker spoke from the dry doorway. The repaired cap reduced repeated night watching, and he might lose regular extra hours after the current term. The upstream landing offered two occasional shifts, which he had not yet accepted. He wanted the bank to stop describing every saved cost as if nobody had earned it. Luo entered that consequence in the closing plan and offered him the actual future task notices. She could not manufacture the same income from the twenty-four just paid or the already assigned repair order.

canal_p08_021.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_021.text: The food stallholder gave her offered batch record and described unsold morning buns during the gate stop. The trustees accepted the document for the later bounded loss review without promising that every unsold bun was compensable. Han's customer would also report his actual transfer expense, if he wanted it heard. Yue expected people to resent the lack of immediate awards. Some did. The stallholder was relieved that the original record would be copied rather than kept from her kitchen, where tomorrow's ordinary batch still needed its own account.

canal_p08_022.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_022.text: The drain householder presented the two winter bills and the current emptied basin. The present repair was complete; the old damage had multiple possible contributors. The council assigned a specific comparison of dates, maintenance logs and the platform alteration for the later review. Han agreed to supply his offered alteration records. The householder said she would preserve her copies and attend the named date. Yue felt the difference between extending a real investigation and giving somebody another indefinite place to wait. The date made the unfinished work more demanding for everyone.

canal_p08_023.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_023.text: Tian proposed an ordinary new-job board with tasks, rates, practical requirements and private replies. A trustee wanted households assigned one turn each so the bank could guarantee labor. The original service pledge could not supply that new assignment. The bank could invite paid applicants and price unfilled tasks, while households could choose collective help under an actual new agreement if they wanted. The trustee disliked how uncertain that sounded. Bao said pretending to have hands did not lift a gate when nobody arrived. The room understood that better after this week's work.

canal_p08_024.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_024.text: The remaining ordinary repair days were listed by worker and task, with completed accepted hours distinguished from future shifts. Yue's twelve-day allocation stayed inside the fifty-six-copper labor line. The other sixteen days included Bao, Jiang, An Ru, the hired tow workers, Tian and the qualified stone worker. Their future field work needed genuine available days rather than a fresh free workforce drawn from the canceled successor list. Pei asked each present applicant to check only the tasks actually offered to them, leaving absent people their own reply route.

canal_p08_025.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_025.text: Han presented the proposed private gear lease, with two usable cargo intervals, current load limits and maintenance duties on his own loading plot. The bank needed those services only if the lease remained cheaper or more dependable than its actual alternatives. The trustees requested one week of ordinary service observations before accepting the later four-copper monthly arrangement. Han agreed. His fifty-six loan claim remained separate from that future lease decision. Yue saw him accept a condition over his own gear without trying to put it back onto the canal's bed.

canal_p08_026.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_026.text: The shower eased before noon. A woman opened the store door and found the yard steaming in pale sunlight. The accepted decisions could be posted, but the trustees still needed the replies about work and loss review gathered accurately. Han wanted his paid acknowledgment and correction carried to the people who doubted it. The householder wanted the actual investigation appointment written on her copy. Tian wanted help turning the new job proposal into invitations people could decline. Yue could support one task while the clerks completed the others.

canal_p08_027.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_027.text: Pei separated the three follow-up stacks by their receivers. One would carry the canceled sale and paid loan installment, one would carry the bounded loss-review appointments, and one would invite applicants for actual remaining repair work. No stack could lend its authority to another merely because the hearing had produced them together. Yue looked through the doorway at the puddles reflecting an ordinary blue sky. The bank had made real decisions. The next question was how those decisions would change what people did after leaving the crowded room.

canal_p08_028.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_028.text: The chair closed the completed decision session and left the store open for the chosen follow-up conversations. Luo returned to the lock because a boat waited at the posted ordinary mark. Han sat with his private purse and an amended notice. The drain householder held her sweet tin. Tian spread the new task sheet over a dry crate. Yue could go with the decision copies, help set the actual loss-review visits or listen to applicants deciding how much of their own time they wanted to offer.

canal_p08_029.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_029.text: The hearing had paid twenty-four, left fifty-six valid and removed the public-bed and successor-service sale. Those actions would stand whichever follow-up Yue chose. She could carry the bounded decisions with Han, arrange the loss review with the householder or help Tian invite actual workers. Each path would reveal a different kind of unfinished business. Outside, the gate moved under Luo's ordinary hand mechanism, and the repaired canal began earning a day that no resolution could guarantee would be simple.

choices.text: Carry the amended decisions with Han.
Help Tian invite present paid workers.

canal_p08_030.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_030.text: Han carried the first amended copy to the widow's blanket stall. She read his signed withdrawal before looking at the paid installment. He said the public twenty-four had reduced a valid monetary debt, not bought another seasonal turn from her family. She already understood the words and asked why he felt obliged to explain them again. He said he feared people would hear only that the bank paid him. She gave the copy back after choosing the sentence she wanted the clerk to read at the counter.

canal_p08_031.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_031.text: At the stall, a customer asked whether the widow's husband had finally been repaid for his replacement days. The old receiving correction acknowledged his work but did not create a new cash award. The widow answered for herself and showed the separate public loan account. Yue realized how readily a hearing's one transfer could become every person's imagined refund. Han let the widow speak without correcting her tone. The useful thing he could carry today was the actual amended claim, not a purse that made every history whole.

canal_p08_032.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_032.text: The next copy went to the former voluntary-list worker who had refused a cheerful account of the founding pledge. He read Han's correction and said the completed release mattered, while his father's famine still mattered too. Han began to explain the timber again, then asked whether the man wanted anything added to the public reply. He wanted the offered account kept without another argument over gratitude. Han agreed. Yue watched a conversation end before either side had won the other's interpretation of an old hard winter.

canal_p08_033.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_033.text: At a doorway, a new tenant worried that the correction applied only to descendants named in the hearing. Yue showed the completed collective provision and removed successor lot. Present residence did not create the old duty either. The tenant could apply for current paid work or decline it under the new notice. Han said that plainly because his own seal had helped create the mistaken claim. The woman thanked him for the correction, then asked him to stop leaving private cargo against her wall. He went to move it.

canal_p08_034.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_034.text: Moving the light empty crates took Han and a store worker only a few minutes. They set them inside his private loading boundary, clear of the tenant's doorway and the ordinary public path. Yue helped point out the marked line without turning the new complaint into an indictment of every old bill. The tenant came outside afterward to inspect the result. She said the hearing now felt real. Han looked almost offended by how small a proof she needed, then laughed and said he wished every remaining problem came in empty crates.

canal_p08_035.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_035.text: The sale supporter met them by the drain house and asked whether Han would still sell his private shed. He had not decided. The main crane would remain if he returned the deposit under the current plan; the unused hoist and spare extension stock might go instead. She said private investment still had a place on the bank. Tian would disagree with her tone, Yue thought, but not necessarily the statement. Han said he wanted his place to be an actual business, which the failed whole-canal sale had not achieved.

canal_p08_036.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_036.text: The buyer's agent caught up with them at the public board. He delivered his own copy of the failed-title finding to the proposed buyer by booked messenger. His report preserved the refundable forty-eight deposit and specified private security. Yue asked him to keep the expired household service out of every future price estimate. He said the corrected schedule already did. She checked the offered public paragraph and found it accurate. A person she disliked could complete an honest action, and the completed action deserved the same careful reading as everyone else's.

canal_p08_037.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_037.text: Han chose not to announce his broker alternatives while delivering the public correction. The private claim sale was still a decision he had not made. At the counter, he asked the clerk to post the actual fifty-six remaining under its toll limits rather than the former eighty. The paid installment receipt would remain available for public comparison. Yue kept the signed counterpart with its assigned receiver. The visible amendment gave future questions somewhere to begin, instead of making people guess how a purse leaving the hearing had changed their obligations.

canal_p08_038.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_038.text: The widow returned to the counter before evening and asked for the offered reading she had chosen. Han stood beside the clerk while it was read, then let her add that her family's old work would not be called incomplete again. A nearby pilot asked whether the next levy was already planned. Luo said no levy had been adopted; current tolls and paid tasks remained at their posted terms. Rumor tried to put another price on the day. The board held still long enough for people to ask it directly.

canal_p08_039.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_039.text: Yue finished the decision deliveries with Han's copied correction dry beneath its cover. One household would collect later through its chosen receiver, and the clerk recorded that arrangement. Han went back to his private store carrying less authority and twenty-four actual copper. Yue had seen him move crates, sign a correction and resist another speech about his mother. None of that purchased forgiveness. It made tomorrow's conversations begin from changed actions rather than the unchanged notice he first asked her to read in full.

canal_p08_040.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_040.text: The householder took Yue to the room whose boards had lifted last winter. The present floor was dry after the drain repair, though the wall still held old marks. She pointed to each mark before Yue opened the loss folder. The dates on the two paid repair bills differed, and the family remembered an intervening winter with no paid board replacement. Yue copied that interval as offered memory, not a third bill. The review needed the actual shape of the loss, including what had not been spent.

canal_p08_041.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_041.text: A patch of wall had been painted over after the first damp winter. The householder's eldest son wanted Yue to scrape it and find the original stain. Yue asked whether that would help date the leak, and nobody had a dependable way to interpret the exposed layers today. They left the painted wall intact and used the surviving dated bills, household notes and ordinary maintenance logs. Taking something apart could look investigative while destroying a surface that the family still wanted in its own room.

canal_p08_042.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_042.text: The family kept the damaged boards behind the shed, with a note made during the second replacement. Bao could inspect their ordinary wear at the scheduled comparison, but a board outside could not independently prove which water had touched it years ago. Yue marked its kept location and the offered date. The householder said she knew the canal failed her even if the wood could not speak in court. Yue said the review would hear her account too. Evidence did not require pretending a person was mute until a plank agreed.

canal_p08_043.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_043.text: Han's platform alteration copy named a different winter from the earlier bill. The later access obstruction might have contributed to subsequent neglected maintenance, but it could not explain a repair that preceded it. Yue set the two dates side by side. The householder read them and changed her written claim about the first winter. She disliked having to narrow it, yet she did so before Han could use the error to dismiss everything. Yue admired the care more because the correction cost the woman an argument she had prepared.

canal_p08_044.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_044.text: The second bill coincided with an uncompleted public drain check and the period of restricted platform access. The surviving records supported several contributing failures rather than one exclusive cause. The trustees' later hearing would determine the actual remedy from that evidence and replies. Yue wrote the questions for Bao's current inspection and Han's records. The householder wanted the earliest available meeting, not another seasonal delay. The clerk had offered the fortieth-day loss review after the flood-route work's current schedule, and she accepted it with the right to report any fresh harm sooner.

canal_p08_045.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_045.text: A food stallholder joined them with her own offered batch note. She could not measure all the customers who might have come during the gate stop, but she could show a real unsold batch and reduced next day's baking. Her claim would use those records rather than an imagined full market's profit. The householder said that sounded unfairly small. The stallholder answered that a small real loss was still hers. Yue copied the approved figures and kept the two claims separate beneath their chosen names.

canal_p08_046.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_046.text: Han's customer sent an offered receipt for the actual upstream transfer. It included a private handling service unrelated to the lock closure, which he asked to count as part of the stop's loss. Luo's landing clerk explained the service distinction and marked the disputed portion for reply rather than paying it immediately. Yue saw the loss review grow less tidy as more real expenses arrived. A common remedy would need to distinguish caused costs from costs that merely traveled beside a difficult week.

canal_p08_047.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_047.text: The householder wanted to know who would help her read the review notice if Pei's eyes worsened. The clerk named the ordinary counter receiver and offered a large-column copy now. Yue made that copy while the family moved the old bills back into their sweet tin. It felt like a better promise than saying she would always be present. The notice would survive her departure because its reading route did not depend on remembering the helpful apprentice who first carried it into the room.

canal_p08_048.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_048.text: A child brought the empty basin from the repaired outlet and held it up like a prize. The mother told her it could return to washing beans now. Yue watched the basin become household equipment again rather than permanent evidence of an official visit. She recorded the present dry test before the child took it outside. The current repair gave the family something immediate. The old loss review gave its unanswered complaint a date. Neither needed to consume every object in the room to remain real.

canal_p08_049.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_049.text: Yue returned to the keeper's store with the agreed review dates, narrowed earlier-winter cause claim and offered copies left under their actual permissions. The clerk accepted the comparison questions for the fortieth day. The householder kept her originals and the large-column notice. She had not received a full payment this afternoon, and Yue did not call the appointment compensation. What she had gained was an open drain, a corrected current schedule and a hearing that would have to answer actual dated evidence when its promised day arrived.

canal_p08_050.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_050.text: Tian invited applicants to speak in the dry corner of the store, away from the hearing crowd. The task sheet named ordinary preparation, observation and clearing work, with rates and practical requirements. One woman wanted a morning shift only; a man asked for work after his cargo boat returned. Yue wrote those actual offers without converting them into full-day availability. The listed future repair hours remained within the unspent labor allocation. A useful answer could be shorter than the clean square Tian first drew beside each name.

canal_p08_051.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_051.text: An older worker offered his grandson's whole afternoon before the grandson arrived. Tian left the proposal unaccepted until the actual young man could answer. He came later, embarrassed, and said he wanted to attend the upstream rope examination instead. His grandfather looked hurt, then asked when the examination ended. The bank could hire him another day if a suitable task remained. Yue remembered how often a family had given her future to somebody else while meaning to help. The young man's small refusal changed the applicant sheet.

canal_p08_052.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_052.text: A woman asked whether refusing current work would weaken her household's corrected standing. Tian showed the canceled successor lot and the independent current task notice. No paid application was needed to keep the old completed pledge complete. The woman declined this week's work because her sister was coming home after a long illness. Tian recorded only the refusal and current availability, leaving the private reason out of the public applicant list. Yue heard it because they spoke together, not because the bank needed to publish it.

canal_p08_053.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_053.text: The boatman's daughter asked for actual hauling requirements. Bao's future trial needed experienced line handling and ground observers, but the three ordinary tow days had already been used for the gate job. New field shifts would use the remaining named allocation rather than assume another unpaid rope crew. If a later task required more hands, it would need a separately funded call. Tian showed the current observation option and its limited hours. The daughter chose to inspect the task site first, declining to accept a job on its title alone.

canal_p08_054.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_054.text: An applicant wanted the highest listed rate without the practical check because his family had worked the founding flood. Tian said the present task required present experience, then stopped before turning it into a rebuke about his ancestors. Bao offered the actual light preparation task suited to the man's current skill. He accepted after seeing the work and the same ordinary day rate. The canceled pledge had not canceled his need to earn money. It had changed how the bank would ask him to use his hands.

canal_p08_055.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_055.text: Tian placed her own availability beside the applicants' private replies. She had completed one paid preparation day and would not offer another repair day within that original labor line unless the remaining assignment could genuinely include it. Her stitching work supplied the evening income she preferred. Yue asked whether she regretted not staying with the cap until its final fit. Tian said she liked knowing it worked without having to be present for every useful part. The answer was one Yue still needed to learn.

canal_p08_056.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_056.text: The clerk found that two offers overlapped on the same task while a different clearing hour had no applicant. Tian wanted to ask the first woman to switch automatically. Yue asked her to show the actual new task and timing instead. The woman declined because its hour fell after her boat left. The gap stayed visible. Bao could revise the sequencing within his remaining accepted day, or the bank could fund a later separate task. A completed square was not worth pretending somebody would arrive after her route departed.

canal_p08_057.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_057.text: The man whose check wages would shrink visited the applicant corner and offered a future maintenance interest after his two upstream shifts. No current extra appointment was made. He wanted the bank's next task notice sent to his actual landing rather than left for household representatives to mention. Tian wrote that contact under the chosen receiver. He thanked her for hearing the loss at the meeting and went to inspect the upstream offer. His future remained uncertain, but it had not been handed over to a new tidy list.

canal_p08_058.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_058.text: Bao reviewed the unfilled clearing hour and moved it beside his already accepted observation round, where the ordinary work could be completed safely without another worker. The task sequence now fit actual available staff. He would still stop if the site required a larger operation than the plan allowed. Tian crossed out the empty appointment square rather than filling it with his name as another paid day. Yue saw a small schedule become more honest without purchasing a single extra hour the budget did not have.

canal_p08_059.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_059.text: Tian gave the clerk the actual applicant replies, accepted tasks and remaining contacts. Yue kept the private reasons outside the public work board, as the speakers wanted. The young man went to his rope examination; the woman went to prepare her sister's room. The accepted future workers left with their own task copies. A job invitation had succeeded even when several people said no. The bank would have the hands it actually hired, and the people outside its schedule would keep their own days.

canal_p08_060.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_060.text: At evening, the follow-up stacks returned to their assigned receivers. The amended title and paid installment were posted, the fortieth-day loss-review appointments were delivered, and the actual work replies changed the remaining schedule. Yue knew one set of conversations closely and heard the others from their participants. The hearing's decisions did not depend on her completing every follow-up herself. Luo closed the lock's ordinary evening movement before joining supper, bringing a practical appetite rather than another statement for the record.

canal_p08_061.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_061.text: Han placed the public twenty-four in a separate private envelope marked for returning the deposit. It was his received money now, and the label represented his own plan rather than a new public restriction. He wanted not to spend it on ordinary store costs while the other twenty-four remained to be found. The broker's offer still stood until the eighteenth day. Yue saw the envelope when Han showed it beside the receivable. He was organizing uncertainty into things he could choose, which was different from claiming certainty already belonged to him.

canal_p08_062.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_062.text: The rain's short shower had cooled the yard without raising the canal beyond its ordinary mark. Luo checked the actual reading and entered it, refusing to make the weather either a proved threat or proof that no threat would come. The down-fork gardens' visit remained accepted for the twenty-fourth day. The bounded upper trial would come before that without sending water toward their crops. Bao's current spill-stop plan needed dry preparation on the eighteenth morning, after the private hoist inspection scheduled that day.

canal_p08_063.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_063.text: On the seventeenth morning, the large amended notice went up beside the now-empty sale board. Pei left the old offending notice visible beneath its cancellation copy so people could see exactly what had changed. No household was asked to burn a family receipt for a cleaner conclusion. Han's corrected public claim showed fifty-six remaining under the toll-share terms. The private shed and loading gear still had their own inventory. Yue watched two walkers read the notices together, asking each other questions neither had thought to bring to the hearing.

canal_p08_064.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_064.text: One walker said the bank had won and Han had lost. The other said Han received twenty-four and still held a loan, so perhaps he won instead. Tian passed carrying linen and said she had won her own hours, which she intended to spend on an order due before night. Both men laughed, uncertain whether she was joking. She was, partly. The hearing had different effects because the people in it held different things. Yue followed her to the workroom rather than staying to choose the most satisfying winner.

canal_p08_065.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_065.text: Tian's order was a sail edge for a boat whose owner spoke against the canceled sale. She wanted the work paid at the agreed price regardless of his view. Yue held the light cloth while Tian checked its tension on the frame. The owner arrived to inspect the seam and paid the first portion on time. He said the common bank still needed to prove it could maintain the spill. Tian said she would like proof too. Their transaction finished without requiring a shared opinion about the hearing.

canal_p08_066.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_066.text: The supplier's carrier returned for the clean empty seal pots and delivered the spare fastening packet already within the material purchase. Bao checked its actual count against the sheet, then stored it for later ordinary repair. A child asked whether they could use the packet as a bell because it rattled beautifully. Bao gave him an empty clean pot instead. Yue liked how the bank resumed small material choices after a formal decision. The canceled sale did not make nails and sealing cord appear by themselves.

canal_p08_067.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_067.text: An Ru completed her accepted comparison hours and booked the ordinary return passage. The public office retained its amended records; archive originals had never left their assigned store. She would answer later specific questions through the clerk rather than remain on the bank until every complaint felt better. Yue asked whether leaving ever made her anxious. An Ru said yes, particularly when people mistook a careful hearing for a finished season. She left a clear receiving route and then left herself, which required a different kind of discipline.

canal_p08_068.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_068.text: Before boarding, An Ru read Yue's orchard request draft at Yue's invitation. It asked the matron whether a personal review could be accepted after the canal's closing day, using the retained earlier arrangement rather than a new universal promise. The requested third morning afterward would fit an ordinary two-day journey. An Ru advised booking only after the actual reply and fare were checked. The letter could repair the conversation about a missed visit; it could not itself become the visit. Yue sent it through the paid personal message route.

canal_p08_069.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_069.text: Han's customer payment boat reached the lower landing after noon. The private clerk counted the eight copper against its acknowledgment and gave the carrier the receiving note. The money was now received, rather than merely promised or aboard a boat in somebody's letter. Han added it to his deposit-return envelope, bringing that actual private sum to thirty-two. He still needed sixteen or another lawful private choice before the deadline. Yue heard the satisfied count through the open store door and smiled without moving it into the public account.

canal_p08_070.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_070.text: The broker came for an answer earlier than his offer's expiry. Han said he would wait until Bao inspected the surplus hoist on the eighteenth day. The broker accepted that but would not keep the price beyond the stated afternoon. The private buyer's agent still had the forty-eight contract and failed-title finding. None of the deadlines disappeared because Han had collected eight. Tian said she was beginning to understand why he wore turned cuffs. He said she should begin with his tailor's actual price before diagnosing his whole life.

canal_p08_071.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_071.text: Bao walked the old spill stop that afternoon. Its guide posts remained, but a lower board had warped and a buried outlet corner held dry roots. The first trial could fill only the upper test pocket under the current bounded plan. Water must not pass the temporary lower stop toward the gardens. He marked the necessary preparation and the ground observation positions. Yue could help with the ordinary clean surfaces during her next assigned workday. The canceled labor pledge did not change how heavy a wet board became once it was misplaced.

canal_p08_072.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_072.text: Luo showed Yue the old high-water mark on the keeper's wall, above the present feeder limit. The future repair would not be accepted for that larger head merely because the ordinary gate passed. The high-water route included upstream warning and downstream ground choices they had not finished surveying. Yue traced the dark mark without using qi. It had no voice to tell her who stood here in the founding flood. Han's supported injured leg, Pei's weary first winter and Tian's absent childhood all belonged to different memories below the same stain.

canal_p08_073.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_073.text: The temporary check worker returned from the upstream landing after accepting its two occasional shifts. He still wanted future task notices from the canal and retained the right to speak about his lost recurring hours. Luo entered the actual accepted private work in his offered update, without calling it an equal replacement. Yue thought of every account she had wanted to make whole by finding one neat balancing line. A life could improve in one column and remain poorer in another. The room finally seemed large enough to hold that sentence.

canal_p08_074.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_074.text: Pei opened the narrow missing-name request again when a woman arrived with a possible reference from her mother's cupboard. Its outside number differed by one final mark. Pei kept the offered copy as a possible lead, not the recovered counterfoil. The collective release remained complete regardless. The woman wanted a patient comparison rather than a quick public naming. Yue set an agreed later counter hour with the clerk. The open question would move forward beside the repair, without putting its uncertainty back on twenty-eight present households.

canal_p08_075.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_075.text: After supper, Tian gave Yue the sail order's finished pay note and said she had enough for next month's room rent if the second portion arrived as agreed. Yue congratulated her on the completed seam and actual first payment. Tian said that sounded like Pei speaking. They laughed, then watched the first evening boat take the repaired lock. The lesson had become a joke they could share rather than a lecture repeated at every door. Yue felt closer to her for being allowed to sound ridiculous.

canal_p08_076.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_076.text: Han closed his private store late and stopped beside the empty sale board. He said he had wanted to make the canal's future one transaction because he was tired of living beside a debt no one finished. Yue asked whether he still wanted that. He said yes, sometimes, but the transaction he imagined had contained other people's lives as if they were spare loading stock. The admission was plain and unhappy. She did not rush to reward it. Tomorrow he would sell something he actually owned, if the inspection supported its price.

canal_p08_077.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_077.text: Jiang's note confirmed her next supervised trial day and the apparatus case's current supply record. The six stones still held two hundred sixteen counted units after the bench and gate movement. She would inspect the prepared upper spill frame before accepting any live use. Yue put the note beside her actual workday list and kept personal practice separate. A repaired gate had given the bank current service. The coming channel trial would ask another question, using its own preparation rather than the glow of a successful hearing.

canal_p08_078.speaker: narrator
canal_p08_078.text: At dusk, the awning had dried enough to be folded and returned to its owner's shed. Bao checked its ties before storing them, then went to prepare the ordinary hoist inspection tools for morning. Tian carried her seedling home in a pot whose leaf now held straight. Luo kept the new gate's final reading and Pei locked the amended receiving record. Yue listened to the last cargo footsteps below her room. Tomorrow's work would begin with things that could be chosen, lifted and fitted, after the expired inheritance finally stopped choosing for them.
